w: Rem Koolhaas doesn't design many concert venues, but Lille got one in 1994 when the Dutch architect turned to a 7,000-seat arena inside the new Lille Grand Palais complex. Acoustics, scenography and engineering were all farmed out to specialists - a starchitect's arena built by committee, and it still packs them in.
s: A Rem Koolhaas-designed arena inside Lille Grand Palais
_facts: Multi-purpose indoor arena seating up to 7,000, part of the Lille Grand Palais complex
Designed by architect Rem Koolhaas with Cecil Balmond, inaugurated in 1994
Acoustics by Renz van Luxemburg, scenography by dUCKS scéno, engineering by Arup Group

w: A fur shop on Rue de la Vieille-Comédie turned into a bookstore in 1936 and kept its name anyway - 'Furet' means ferret, a nod to rabbit-hunting with them. The flagship on the Grand Place, opened in 1959, was the largest bookshop on Earth from 1992 to 1999, and it's still one of the biggest in France.
s: The bookshop named after a rabbit-hunting ferret
_facts: Chain of bookstores in the Nord department, tracing back to 1936 when a fur store became a bookshop
Name refers to the local tradition of rabbit hunting with ferrets ('furet')
Flagship store on Lille's Grand Place, established 1959
Was the largest bookstore in the world from 1992 to 1999

w: Founded in 1822, Lille's natural history museum has spent two centuries quietly absorbing other institutions' orphaned collections - ethnographic pieces from the old Musée Moillet, industrial artifacts from the city's defunct Musée Industriel et Commercial. A cabinet of curiosities built one merger at a time.
s: A natural history museum built from other museums' leftovers
_facts: Founded in 1822, houses zoological and geological collections
Holdings enhanced with ethnographic specimens from the Musée Moillet
Also absorbed industrial objects from the old Musée Industriel et Commercial de Lille
